newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sky is the limit for booming Belgian bonds.
newsitem.headline: Sky is the limit for booming Belgian bonds.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds rose sharply as Europe collectively boomed on Friday on a combination of sentiment, technicals and speculation of a German rate cut, and traders said they saw no quick end to the rally.
"It opened a lot higher this morning and then went on from there," one trader said. "There is nothing to stop this market at the moment."

The December futures contract surged 91 basis points to a new closing high of 121.83, and the yield of the benchmark 2006 OLO fell to 5.77 percent from 5.90 with traders talking of it hitting 5.75. The spread over Bunds stayed at 15 basis points.
Traders said there was buying all along the yield curve as shorts covered themselves and turned long.
But they said there was some portfolio selling late in the afternoon, particularly in four-year paper.

The key factor fuelling the pan-European rally seemed to be emerging speculation that Germany might ride to the aid of the French economy and cut short-term interest rates, although traders said they were dubious about it.
"I see no reason why Germany should suddenly break with tradition and help France," one trader said. "It is a dangerous game that people are playing."
But traders said that despite their misgivings there was no point in trying to buck the trend.

"The only thing to stop this market would be disappointment if short-term rates are not cut or if there are poor IFO figures," one trader said. "But in any event that won't happen until the New Year."
